subject: Shiny Server (Open Source) Licensing for Commercial purposes

messages.author: 8cd509597cee391a
messages.subject: Shiny Server (Open Source) Licensing for Commercial purposes
parts:
Hi there,

I am interested in using the R Shiny package to develop R Shiny apps on premises for a client.

I intend to use the Open Source Shiny Server as I will not be having more than 100 users.

What are the licensing terms for this commercial purpose? Also, how secure is the Open Source Shiny Server?

Thank you.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server (Open Source) Licensing for Commercial purposes
parts:
Shiny Server Open Source itself is AGPLv3 licensed. You are under no obligation to redistribute your own Shiny apps, or any packages that the apps use, as AGPL. If you make changes to Shiny Server Open Source, or create another software package that is derived from the code in Shiny Server Open Source, then you must offer the users of your (now-custom) server the source code under the terms of the AGPL.

For security, Shiny Server Open Source does not have built-in authentication (username/password to access an app) nor encryption (https). If you're OK with that and the limitation of a single concurrent R process for each app, then you should be fine with Shiny Server Open Source.
